4	worker in the run. Read it fully before doing anything.
5	
6	## Mission (approved verbatim in essence)
7	
8	Test Fortress's founding claim on the best possible specimen. The claim:
9	the gap between how ML literature states a transformer's mathematics and
10	how programs implement it is a language defect that Fortress was built
11	to close. The specimen: Karpathy's microgpt, the smallest complete GPT.
12	The test: construct, in running and verified Fortress, the notation that
13	lets each building block of the model be stated so that its typeset form
14	and the literature's own formula sit side by side and the reader can
15	judge the distance **by eye**. The deliverable teaches two things at
16	once and inseparably: how a GPT works (a reader starting from zero
17	leaves understanding it) and how the notation is constructed (what the
18	language gives, what it must be taught, and what it cannot yet say).
19	Where the correspondence fails, the failure is shown and classified —
20	implementation gap (revival worklist) versus design limit. Everything
21	shown runs; correctness is anchored to the Python reference; the
22	process is documented.
23	
24	**Not the mission** (named local minima — do not fall into them):
25	fidelity to Steele's 2015 slide idioms; preservation of any prior
26	rung's code structure (this iteration starts FROM SCRATCH); the golden
27	check as an aesthetic constraint (it is a correctness instrument only);
28	interpreter speed (measured, reported, never steering notation).
29	
30	## Standing design rules (from Pavol, binding)
31	
32	1. **No custom BIG operators** (`BIG OPLUS`, `BIG BOXPLUS`, any new
33	   glyph) unless the form is (a) genuinely the prevalent way ML
34	   literature writes that mathematics, or (b) provably the only working
35	   way in current Fortress, with the spec-vs-implementation gap
36	   documented. The ML literature writes Σ, Π, 𝔼, max — never custom big
37	   operators. Glyph imitation of Σ is not Σ. Default: named functions
38	   (`sum(...)`) over comprehensions; the genuine library `SUM` where
39	   summands are `Number`s (e.g. over `.data` inside a sum-node
40	   constructor).
41	2. **The specification is the first authority** for any language
42	   question: `Specification/` LaTeX sources (byte-identical to
43	   1.0-frozen in all chapters audited so far). Order of authority:
44	   spec → `explorations/expressiveness-review.md` (audited findings
45	   with probes) → library sources → fresh empirical probe. Never end a
46	   design path at the first interpreter error: check what the spec
47	   sanctions (the vector×matrix "impossibility" had a documented
48	   escape, the Meet Rule / `excludes`), then record divergence.
49	3. **No single-data-point rules.** Any claimed constraint ("always
50	   parenthesize X", "Y is impossible") requires either a spec citation
51	   or two independent probes, recorded.
52	
53	## Verified facts (do not re-derive; probes in `explorations/spec-probes/`)
54	
55	- List/comprehension element-type ascriptions `[\T\]` are needed ONLY
56	  when elements' runtime class differs from the target (numeric
57	  literals → `FloatLiteral`; nested `ArrayList[\…\]` under invariant

59	  they are redundant. Return types on definitions are optional
60	  (inference chapter in the spec is a stub; the implementation infers).
61	  The `zip` static argument is mandatory.
62	- The algebraic tower that exists: `AdditiveGroup[\T\]` and
63	  `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]` only (`FortressLibrary.fss:328,340`).
64	  Extending `MultiplicativeRing[\V\]` with `one`/`TIMES` inherits

68	  `Library/incomplete/…INCOMPLETE`.

70	  are illegal — but **mutually excluding carrier traits make both
71	  directions legal** (library's own Vector/Matrix at
72	  `FortressLibrary.fss:2634,2641` via `Rank1 excludes Rank2`; probes

49	## Block-by-block: distance to the literature, judged on the render
50	
51	**rmsnorm** — paper: `RMSNorm(x) = x / sqrt(x·x/d + eps)`. Render:
52	
53	    s = sqrt((x·x)/|x| + 0.00001)
54	    ⟨ u/s | u ← x ⟩

56	The radical line is near-verbatim (the radical, `x·x`, `|x|` for d, the
57	literal ε). Two departures: the elementwise division is a comprehension,
58	not `x/s`; and it is two lines, not one. Probe P1 verified the true
59	one-liner (`⟨ u / sqrt((x·x)/|x| + eps) | u ← x ⟩`) runs with
60	*identical* forward values and gradients — but it rebuilds the norm
61	subgraph once per element (d× tape nodes), so the hoisted form is the
62	honest graph-faithful rendering; Karpathy's reference also hoists.
63	
64	**softmax** — paper: `softmax(a)_j = e^(a_j) / Σ_k e^(a_k)`. Render: four
65	short lines (max shift, exp comprehension, `z = sum(w)`, `⟨ u/z | u ← w ⟩`).
66	Furthest from its formula of the four blocks, but each line is one paper
67	notion, and the `.data` in the max shift is faithful to the reference
68	(Karpathy also takes `max(v.data ...)` — the shift is numerics, not
69	mathematics; `softmax(a) = softmax(a − c)` is an identity).
70	
71	**attend** — paper: `A_j = q·k_j / sqrt(d_k); p = softmax(A); out = Σ_j p_j v_j`.
72	Render:
73	
74	    p = softmax(⟨ (q·k)/√|q| | k ← ks ⟩)
75	    ⟨ sum(⟨ p_j ((vs_j)[c]) | j ← 0#|p| ⟩) | c ← 0#|vs₀| ⟩

77	The score line is the closest line in the file to its literature form —
78	a reader of "Attention is All You Need" recognizes it instantly, with the
79	comprehension standing where the matrix product `qKᵀ` stands. The blend
80	is where minimalism genuinely breaks: the vector form `Σ_j p_j v_j`
81	needs scalar×vector (one more aggregate overload) plus a vector-valued
82	big sum (a registration or a `vecsum` function); in this budget the
83	blend is the *index* form `out_c = Σ_j p_j v_{j,c}` — which the
84	literature also writes, but as the definition one level down. The
85	`(vs_j)[c]` bracket noise is forced (chained subscripts, below).
86	
87	**ffn** — paper: `FFN(x) = W₂ relu(W₁ x)`. Render:
88	`matvec(w₂, relu(matvec(w₁, x)))`. Structure identical (composition,
89	pointwise relu); the whole distance is the word `matvec` where the paper
90	juxtaposes. This is the block that most visibly pays for the budget.

92	## Deviations, classified
93	
94	1. **Elementwise vector ops as comprehensions** (`⟨u/s | u ← x⟩`,
95	   `⟨exp(u−c) | u ← a⟩`, and in the full model `vadd`) —
96	   *deliberate-with-reason* (the one-overload budget). Not a language
97	   limit: the prior rung runs `/(List,V)`, `+(List,List)` etc. legally.
98	2. **`matvec(...)` instead of `W x`** — *deliberate-with-reason* (same
99	   budget). Not a language limit; `opr juxtaposition(List[\List[\V\]\],
100	   List[\V\])` coexists with `DOT` legally (prior rung proves it; the
101	   Meet-Rule conflict is only between two juxtapositions on (List,List)
102	   shapes).
103	3. **Σ as the named function `sum`** — *doubly justified*: the plan's
104	   standing rule 1 makes named `sum(...)` the default, and the genuine
105	   library `SUM` is sealed against user types three ways (Number seal,
106	   no-static-param-overloading, one-nullary-registration-per-name —
107	   verified facts; the seal itself is an *implementation gap* on the
108	   revival worklist). Inside `sum`'s constructor the genuine library
109	   `SUM` folds the `.data`s, as rule 1 sanctions.
110	4. **`(vs[j])[c]`** — *design limit*: chained subscripts are
111	   ungrammatical by design (`Specification` concrete-syntax.tex:921,
112	   already adjudicated in `explorations/expressiveness-review.md`). The
113	   render shows `(vs_j)[c]` where the paper writes `v_{j,c}`.
114	5. **`u.data` in softmax's max** — *deliberate-with-reason*: mirrors the
115	   Python reference line-for-line; the shift is numerics.
116	6. **Index-form blend instead of `Σ_j p_j v_j`** —
117	   *deliberate-with-reason* (budget; see frontier). Note the vector form
118	   under a custom glyph (`BIG BOXPLUS`) is what standing rule 1 exists
119	   to forbid: the literature writes Σ, and Σ-for-vectors is exactly what
120	   the sealed library denies (implementation gap), so the honest choices
121	   are the index form (taken) or a named `vecsum`.
122	7. **Falsified precaution**: comprehension-body parens around
123	   `(q DOT k) / SQRT |q|` — probe P2 shows the unparenthesized body
124	   parses and computes correctly even with `|q|` before the generator
125	   `|`. Dropped everywhere; do not propagate the "protect the body"
126	   habit to iteration 2.

129	
130	Ranked by correspondence gained per line added (all verified runnable —
131	the prior rung runs them; nothing here is blocked by the language):
132	
133	1. `opr /(x: List[\V\], s: V)` — **1 line** → rmsnorm becomes the
134	   verbatim one-liner `x / SQRT((x DOT x)/|x| + eps)` and softmax's last
135	   line becomes `w / z`. The best line in the whole design space.
136	2. `opr juxtaposition(w: List[\List[\V\]\], x: List[\V\])` — **1 line**
137	   → `ffn = w₂ relu(w₁ x)` verbatim; every projection becomes `wq x`.
138	3. `opr +(x: List[\V\], y: List[\V\])` — **1 line** → `h0 = wte[t] +
139	   wpe[i]` and both residuals verbatim.
140	4. Scalar×vector juxtaposition + a vector-valued big sum — **~10 lines**
141	   (juxt(V,List) + vecsum + monoid object + registered glyph) → the
142	   blend as `Σ_j p_j v_j`. Worst ratio, and the glyph half runs into
143	   standing rule 1.
144	5. Excluding carrier objects (Vec/Mat à la `p7_excludes`/`p14_genwrap`)
145	   — **~12+ lines** → both juxtaposition directions at once, `|x|`,
146	   generator integration. Needed only when you want vector×matrix AND
147	   matrix×vector; nothing in microgpt does.

150	operator became four, and every block except the blend and softmax's
151	interior is the paper line verbatim. That is, I believe, the actual
152	frontier of this design space: **three cheap overloads separate "the
153	reader recognizes every block" from "the reader recognizes half of each
154	block"; everything beyond them buys single lines at 10× the price.**
